problem: Leaders wanted to reduce internal conflict and keep the company focused on its work.
title: Basecamp bans societal and political discussions on its internal platform
context: Basecamp's CEO announced new policies on 26 April 2021 after internal disputes.
decision_made: Bar societal and political discussions on company platforms, stop taking public positions on unrelated political issues, and offer severance to those who did not want to stay.
action_taken: Offered severance of up to six months for staff with more than three years and three months for others.
observed_outcome: Reports said 18 of 57 employees, about a third, took the severance. The CEO later apologised for the handling but said the new policies stood.
lessons: A policy that narrows employee voice can trigger a large voluntary exit even when severance is generous.
limitations: Figures come from press reports, and longer-term business effects were not found. The policy and handling were criticised separately.

claims.claim_text: Basecamp's CEO barred societal and political discussions from the company's internal platform on 26 April 2021.
Reports said 18 of 57 employees took the severance package, and the policies stood after an apology.
